paragraphs: I'm applying for the FP&A Analyst role at Insomnia Cookies. I'm an MBA Finance (STEM) candidate at Fordham Gabelli, and before that I worked at JPMorgan Asset Management, Lenovo and Thomson Reuters. What interests me is that this role goes past reporting. Questions about labor, pricing and new bakery openings are concrete decisions, and the analysis either helps an operator make a better call or it doesn't.

At Lenovo I built forecasts and scenario analyses on capital allocation that improved capital efficiency by 15%, and ran variance and sensitivity analyses on budget changes. At Thomson Reuters I supported monthly P&L forecasting, variance analysis and close for the ANZ region, and worked on cash flow analysis and reconciliation. At JPMorgan Asset Management I worked on budget allocation across marketing channels and benchmarked past allocations, which identified 30% in efficiency gains.

That maps to the budgeting, monthly reporting and business partnering you describe. My background is corporate rather than restaurant or retail finance, so bakery-level economics would be new to me, and I'd start by learning how the shops run. I'd bring strong Excel habits, and I'm comfortable asking why a number moved and explaining the answer plainly. I'd welcome the chance to talk.
